//: Our own catalogue rows and the RepDB row each one supersedes. Re-seeding re-inserts every one of these, so the generator emits the clean-up at the end of the same file rather than leaving it to a migration somebody has to remember. Each pairing was read as a MOVEMENT, not as a string.

our_own_duplicates.triceps-pushdown: one movement filed twice; src/lib/machines.ts names the singular 'Tricep Pushdown'

//name_matters: The NAME is recorded alongside the id because the clean-up cannot rely on the id alone. The same file re-keys RepDB rows to the slug of their name, so a twin that survived one run comes back under a DIFFERENT id — 'squat' becomes 'barbell-back-squat' — and a delete keyed on 'squat' then matches nothing while the duplicate sits there. That is how four duplicates survived three rounds of clean-up. A name does not move.
